section_1.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Fourier Perspective
section_1.content: Briefly define a signal as a combination of simple waves (sines/cosines). Introduce the two domains: Time (when it happens) and Frequency (what notes it contains). Establish that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between them.
section_1.example: Visualize a music box: The 'Time' domain shows the sequence of notes being played; the 'Frequency' domain shows the sheet music notation of the specific pitches.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Narrow vs. Broad
section_2.content: Explain that 'narrowing' a signal in one domain necessarily 'spreads' it in the other. Use a graphical representation showing a tall, thin spike in the time domain becoming a flat, wide plateau in the frequency domain.
section_2.example: Imagine a camera shutter: If you take a photo with a 'narrow' exposure time (a blink), you capture the 'where' but lose the motion information (frequency) of the subject.

section_3.title: The Mathematical Bound
section_3.content: Introduce the Heisenberg-Gabor Inequality: Δt · Δf ≥ 1/(4π). Explain that we cannot shrink both uncertainty windows simultaneously. The product has a hard floor—a limit imposed by the nature of wave math.
section_3.example: An animated 'energy box' that cannot be squeezed smaller than a fixed area; pushing the sides in (time) forces the top and bottom to expand (frequency).

section_4.title: Real-World Application: The Bat's Chirp
section_4.content: Demonstrate why this matters. A bat needs to locate prey (timing) but also identify prey type (frequency). Explain the trade-off bats make in their sonar pulses to balance precision in both domains.
section_4.example: Show a bat emitting a 'Short Click' (Great time resolution, poor frequency resolution) vs. a 'Long Whistle' (Great frequency resolution, poor time resolution) as they approach an insect.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap that the Uncertainty Principle isn't a flaw in our instruments, but a fundamental property of waves. Conclude with the importance of 'Optimal Windows' in signal processing.
section_5.example: The 'Signal Engineering Seesaw': Balancing the time-frequency trade-off to get the best of both worlds for radar, music, and quantum mechanics.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
